channel.title: SecuBuzz · Cybersecurity News Briefs
channel.description: Fast, factual 60-word cybersecurity briefs and CISA KEV alerts for security professionals.

item.title: Red Hat Issues Critical PHP 8.3 Security Update
item.description: Red Hat released a critical security update for the php:8.3 module on RHEL 9, addressing multiple vulnerabilities. The update is rated Critical, with CVSS base scores provided for each vulnerability via the referenced CVE links, indicating high-severity flaws. Apply the patch promptly; no workarounds are available, and the update should be deployed across all affected systems.

item.title: Red Hat Releases Kernel Security Update for RHEL 8.6
item.description: Red Hat issued a kernel security update for RHEL 8.6 Advanced Mission Critical Update Support and Extended Update Support Long-Life Add-On, addressing multiple vulnerabilities. The update carries an Important impact rating, with CVSS base scores available for each vulnerability via the referenced CVE links. Security teams should apply the patch immediately to mitigate potential exploitation; no workarounds are currently recommended.

item.title: Microsoft Confirms Printing Issues on Forcepoint Systems
item.description: Microsoft confirmed that the KB5132043 Windows 11 hotpatch caused printing failures on systems running Forcepoint DLP software. The issue does not represent a security vulnerability but disrupts print functionality for affected users. Microsoft advises users to postpone the hotpatch until a fix is released or to revert to a previous Windows 11 build.

item.title: Signal Blocks AI Assistants From Accessing Private Messages
item.description: Signal updated its app to block AI assistants on iOS 27 and Android, preventing them from capturing users’ private message content. The change stops assistants like Siri and Google Gemini from reading the screen to answer queries, protecting data stores. No vulnerability is reported; the update is a privacy safeguard that requires installing the latest Signal version.

item.title: AI-Assisted Attacks Trigger Unauthorized Bank Transfers
item.description: AI-assisted threat actors targeted Indian ICT assets, forcing unauthorized financial transfers at banks and fintech firms. The attacks leveraged machine-learning-driven phishing and credential-stealing techniques, exploiting known login-bypass flaws to move laterally within banking networks. Red CERT-In urges immediate patching of vulnerable systems and enhanced monitoring of transaction logs to detect further unauthorized activity.

item.title: BADBOX 3.0 TV Boxes Generate 40 Billion Ad Requests
item.description: BADBOX 3.0 infected low-cost TV boxes produced roughly 40 billion ad bid requests daily, exceeding 4% of all connected TV traffic. The malware hijacked ad rendering processes, enabling stealthy traffic injection without user awareness and creating a large-scale advertising fraud network.

item.title: Bulgarian Government Breach Exposes 62 Million Pages
item.description: Hackers accessed Bulgarian state administration networks for five years, exfiltrating 130 GB of documents. The intrusion leveraged covert persistence mechanisms to download over 62 million pages, representing a significant compromise of sensitive government data. Bulgarian authorities disrupted the operation and are investigating the breach; no vendor patch is applicable, but organizations should review network segmentation and intrusion detection controls.

item.title: Weekly Security Roundup: Nov 16-22
item.description: Malwarebytes Labs released a weekly security roundup covering topics from Nov 16 to Nov 22, 2026. The report summarizes emerging threats, vulnerability disclosures, and defensive recommendations observed during that period, including zero-day exploits and supply-chain risks. The summary is available for security teams to review trends, update defenses, and threat intelligence.

item.title: Red Hat Kernel Update for RHEL 10.0 EUS
item.description: Red Hat released a kernel update for Enterprise Linux 10.0 Extended Update Support, addressing multiple security issues. The advisory notes an Important security impact, with CVSS base scores linked to each vulnerability, indicating potential high-severity flaws. Security teams should apply the update immediately to mitigate the identified kernel vulnerabilities, as no workarounds are provided.

item.title: CISA Alerts on Cisco Expressway RCE Exploitation
item.description: CISA reports that attackers are exploiting a recently patched critical vulnerability in Cisco Expressway, enabling remote code execution. The flaw, classified as critical, allows unauthenticated users to execute arbitrary code, and has been actively leveraged in the wild. Cisco has released a patch; security teams must apply it immediately and monitor for exploitation attempts.

item.title: Malicious Ad Domains Steal iPhone Crypto Recovery Phrases
item.description: Hackers leveraged over 480 malicious ad domains to compromise iPhones and exfiltrate crypto wallet recovery phrases, passwords, and personal data. The MoldyRoost operation exploited ad rendering engine flaws, enabling credential theft without user interaction across 47+ countries. Apple issued a security advisory urging iOS updates and users to avoid suspicious ads; security teams should monitor ad traffic and enforce sandboxing.

item.title: Red Hat Kernel Update for RHEL 8
item.description: Red Hat issued a kernel update for Enterprise Linux 8, addressing several security issues. The advisory labels the update as Important, with CVSS base scores linked to each vulnerability, implying high-severity flaws. Apply the update promptly to remediate the kernel vulnerabilities; no workarounds are provided, and ensure system integrity today.

item.title: Red Hat Kernel-rt Update for RHEL 8

item.title: Cancer Institute Tackles Shadow IT in Research
item.description: Istituto Nazionale Tumori (INT) discusses how to keep a cancer research hospital operational while protecting against cyberattacks. The director explains collaboration with partner hospitals in the Rare Cancer Network, challenges when staff cannot access chemotherapy plans, and why banning shadow IT rarely fixes gaps. INT also highlights the most burdensome EU regulation and outlines its approach to secure research workflows.

item.title: Xalgorix Introduces AI-Powered Pen Testing Tool
item.description: Xalgorix, an open-source AI penetration testing framework, validates findings through a dual-agent verification process. The primary agent identifies potential bugs, while a secondary agent attempts to exploit them; failures to confirm a bug result in a flagged finding for manual review, reducing false positives. The tool is available for community use and encourages reviewers to assess flagged vulnerabilities before reporting.

item.title: Early Black Friday Scams Emerge Without Red Flags
item.description: Scammers began posting fake Black Friday deals on September 1, earlier than last year, rarely referencing the holiday or using familiar domain names. The campaigns appear as Facebook group posts or Google Sites pages, mimicking retailer sale language promoting software, payment, travel, or crypto offers. Security teams should monitor social media and verify vendor legitimacy before engaging with such promotions.

The advisory references multiple CVEs with CVSS base scores, but no active exploitation is reported, and the update is classified as Important by Product Security. Administrators should apply the Cockpit patch promptly to address the identified vulnerabilities.

item.description: ISACA released COBIT 7, the latest version of its governance framework, adding AI risk scenarios. Security teams should review the new scenarios and integrate them into their governance and risk management processes.

Administrators should apply the fence-agents update immediately and verify that the affected services are restarted to enforce the new security controls.

item.title: Matilda Sells Claimed VMware vCenter Exploit
item.description: A forum seller named Matilda is offering a claimed exploit for VMware vCenter Server, targeting CVE-2026-123890. The critical vulnerability would let an attacker create a new vCenter administrator account, but no confirmed exploitation has been reported. Broadcom issued a patch on November 19, 2026; administrators should apply it immediately to mitigate the risk.

item.title: Curl Receives Moderate Security Update

The patch fixes several vulnerabilities that could lead to remote code execution or information disclosure, as reflected in the CVSS scores. System administrators should install the curl update promptly and restart any services that depend on it to apply the security fixes.

item.title: RHEL 9 Thunderbird Update Fixes Code Execution Flaws
item.description: Red Hat issued an important security update for Thunderbird on RHEL 9, fixing vulnerabilities that could lead to memory corruption or arbitrary code execution. The patch addresses CVE-linked defects with a CVSS score in the moderate range, and no active exploitation has been observed. Users should install RHSA-2026:102170 promptly to secure their mail clients.

item.title: RHEL 8 xdg-desktop-portal Update Addresses Privilege Escalation
item.description: Red Hat released an important security update for xdg-desktop-portal on RHEL 8, addressing multiple vulnerabilities that could allow privilege escalation or code execution. The update includes patches for CVE-linked flaws, with a CVSS base score indicating moderate to high risk, but no active exploitation reported. Security teams should apply the RHSA-2026:102175 update immediately to mitigate potential attacks.

item.title: Red Hat Updates libgsf for Security
item.description: Red Hat released a security update for libgsf on RHEL 10.2 EUS, addressing multiple vulnerabilities identified by CVE references. The flaws involve improper handling of GSF files, potentially allowing remote code execution via crafted documents. Red Hat has issued a patch; administrators should apply the update immediately to mitigate exploitation.

item.title: git-lfs Security Update for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10
item.description: Red Hat released a security update for git-lfs on Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10, addressing a vulnerability that could allow code execution. The flaw, referenced by multiple CVEs, permits attackers to inject malicious content during file transfer operations, potentially compromising system integrity. Red Hat recommends applying the latest git-lfs package immediately to mitigate the risk, with no additional workarounds required.

item.title: Red Hat issues nodejs22 important security update
item.description: An important-impact flaw in Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10.0’s nodejs22 runtime was found, enabling remote code execution via malformed JavaScript objects. The vulnerability, with a high CVSS score, permits attackers to execute arbitrary code without authentication, though no public exploits are known. Red Hat has issued a nodejs22 update; security teams must install the patch promptly to prevent potential compromise.

item.title: Red Hat releases glib2 moderate security update
item.description: A moderate-impact vulnerability in Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8.8’s glib2 library was identified, affecting SAP and Telecommunications Update Services via untrusted input handling. The flaw, rated CVSS moderate, allows local privilege escalation if exploited, but no active exploitation has been reported. Red Hat has released a patch; administrators should apply the glib2 update immediately to mitigate the risk.

item.title: Red Hat Releases xdg-desktop-portal Update for RHEL 10.2
item.description: Red Hat issued a security update for xdg-desktop-portal on RHEL 10.2 Extended Update Support, addressing multiple vulnerabilities. The patch mitigates potential remote code execution and privilege escalation flaws in the portal's sandboxed application handling, with CVSS scores ranging from moderate to high. Red Hat recommends applying the update immediately to secure affected systems.

item.title: Red Hat Releases xdg-desktop-portal Security Update
item.description: Red Hat issued a security update for xdg-desktop-portal on RHEL 9.4 for SAP Solutions, addressing multiple vulnerabilities. Red Hat recommends applying the update immediately to secure affected systems.

item.title: QEMU KVM MA Flaw Allows Local Privilege Escalation
item.description: Red Enterprise Linux 7 Extended Lifecycle Support users face a qemu-kvm-ma flaw that may enable local privilege escalation via the virtual machine monitor. The vulnerability stems from improper memory mapping handling, and Red Hat rates it Moderate with a CVSS base score in the CVE references. Apply the qemu-kvm-ma update immediately; no workaround exists until the patch is installed.

item.title: GNOME Remote Desktop Vulnerability Enables Remote Code Execution
item.description: Red Enterprise Linux 9.8 Extended Update Support users face a gnome-remote-desktop flaw that permits remote code execution via the remote desktop protocol. The issue arises from unchecked input during session negotiation, and Red Hat rates it Important with a CVSS base score in the CVE references. Apply the gnome-remote-desktop update immediately; no workaround exists until the patch is installed.

item.title: Red Hat Issues Security Update for xdg-desktop-portal
item.description: Red Hat released a security update for the xdg-desktop-portal component in Red Enterprise Linux 10, addressing multiple vulnerabilities. The update mitigates flaws that could allow privilege escalation or unauthorized data access, with CVSS scores provided in the CVE references. Administrators should apply the RHSA-2026:102177 update immediately to ensure protection against the identified weaknesses.

item.title: Volkswagen Cars Exposed via Bluetooth Spy Flaws
item.description: Researchers demonstrated that Bluetooth flaws in Volkswagen vehicles enable eavesdropping on conversations and GPS tracking. The flaws grant unauthorized cabin control and location access, exposing private data and enabling remote manipulation, with a 16-month exposure after disclosure. Volkswagen should expedite the release of a patch and advise owners to disable Bluetooth or apply the fix immediately to mitigate the risk.

item.title: OpenAI Finds Zero-Day Mobile OS Bypass and RCE
item.description: OpenAI’s GPT-6.2 Astra discovered zero-day flaws in a popular mobile OS and a common network service. The flaws include a permission-bypass exposing private data and a remote code execution path reachable from a low-privileged role. No vendor patch is yet available; security teams should monitor OpenAI advisories and apply any future OS or service updates promptly.

item.title: Red Hat Updates mingw-expat for RHEL8
item.description: Red Hat released an Important security update for mingw-expat on Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8 to fix a kernel-related flaw. The flaw, cited in several CVE references, carries a CVSS base score indicating high severity, but no active exploitation has been reported. The vendor has made the patch available; administrators should apply it immediately to mitigate potential exploitation.

item.title: Cleverbridge Reports Card Data Theft
item.description: Cleverbridge confirmed that attackers exfiltrated payment card data from its e-commerce platform, including card numbers, expiration dates, and CVV codes. The breach involved unauthorized access to the platform’s database, exposing sensitive payment information to malicious actors. Cleverbridge has begun notifying affected customers and is investigating the incident; affected users should monitor accounts for fraudulent activity.

item.title: Red Hat gfs2-utils security update released
item.description: Red Hat released a gfs2-utils update for Enterprise Linux 9, fixing a flaw that could allow arbitrary code via malformed GFS2 metadata. The issue stems from improper handling of GFS2 superblock fields, with a CVSS base score indicating moderate impact; no active exploitation observed. Apply the patch through the standard update channel to mitigate the risk.

item.title: Red Hat libgsf security update released

The issue stems from insufficient validation of GSF headers, with a CVSS base score indicating important impact; no active exploitation reported. Apply the patch via the standard update channel to mitigate the risk.
